name: cheaper-travelling
what_it_holds: Apache Spark + Kafka streaming pipeline that pulls from Skyscanner, GeoDB Cities, and Flixbus public APIs to compare multimodal travel costs (flights, buses). Academic/course project; MIT licensed, 12 stars. No committed historical dataset, a live-streaming architecture demo.
why_useful: A concrete example of pulling live Skyscanner fare data via API into a structured pipeline; low value as-is (no stored data, small project) but a usable reference architecture if the team wants to build its own Skyscanner-API puller.
themes: Airline fare tracking datasets (Google Flights scrapers, Skyscanner, Hopper reports), airfare price indices
why_all: A concrete example of pulling live Skyscanner fare data via API into a structured pipeline; low value as-is (no stored data, small project) but a usable reference architecture if the team wants to build its own Skyscanner-API puller.

name: subway_ridership
what_it_holds: Python scripts (`bart_ridership.py`, `mta_ridership.py`) plus a committed `output_data/` folder of processed CSVs (daily ridership time series, busiest-station rankings) for BART and NYC MTA, built for COVID-era before/after comparison against a Feb-1 baseline; BART updates monthly, MTA weekly at source.
why_useful: Ready-made daily NYC and SF-Bay-Area transit volume series usable as a coincident indicator of local mobility/tourism recovery in two ABNB-relevant metros (NYC panel city; SF Bay Area adjacent).
geography: New York City; San Francisco Bay Area
themes: Public transit ridership and airport rail links (MTA, TfL, RATP, JR) as visitor proxies; ridership open data
why_all: Ready-made daily NYC and SF-Bay-Area transit volume series usable as a coincident indicator of local mobility/tourism recovery in two ABNB-relevant metros (NYC panel city; SF Bay Area adjacent).
